## What this dashboard shows

- This is a demo showing how Snowflake unifies five Wipro group companies running on five different ERPs (two SAP S/4HANA systems, Oracle E-Business Suite, Microsoft Dynamics 365, and Tally) under one reporting structure with one chart of accounts and one set of KPI definitions.
- Only Company 1 (Wipro Consumer Care International) uses real SAP Business Data Cloud data read in place (zero-copy); Companies 2–5 are simulated in their native ERP formats and sized relative to the real SAP company.
- The group structure spans three business segments: Consumer Care & Lighting, Infrastructure Engineering, and Joint Ventures, operating across USA, Australia, Germany, Netherlands and India in multiple currencies (USD, AUD, EUR, INR).

## What to report

- The group operates through 5 companies on 5 different ERP platforms, with data consolidated without moving SAP data via zero-copy integration for the Consumer Care International business.
- Two Joint Venture entities are included: Wipro GE Healthcare (49% ownership) on Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery (51% ownership) on Tally Prime.
- The architecture enables six key finance capabilities: one reporting structure, continuous close, rolling forecast, AI in finance, working capital management, and M&A/JV integration through data landing and mapping rather than ERP re-implementation.
- The platform supports intercompany elimination, INR and USD translation, and unified KPI definitions across all entities and scopes.

## Watch out for

- This is simulated group data sized relative to the real SAP company and not Wipro's actual figures; company names are demo labels only.
- ERP assignments, countries and JV ownership percentages are illustrative only (noted as PRD assumptions A2, A3), so governance mappings may not reflect actual operating structure.
- Only 1 of 5 companies (Wipro Consumer Care International) uses real data; the remaining 4 companies are fully simulated, creating potential data quality and comparability gaps in any cross-company analysis.
- Question to ask: What validation has been performed to ensure the simulated data scaling and JV ownership assumptions produce realistic consolidated results for board reporting?
